summary: Madras School of Economics is a specialist institution founded in Chennai in 1993. Its current taught portfolio includes integrated economics, five MA specialisations, data science and two MBAs. The economics and data-science routes combine quantitative study with applied work, while entry requirements differ by programme and applicant category.
campusLifestyle: The Kotturpuram campus has air-conditioned classrooms, a library with computer and reading facilities, hostels, a mess and a cafeteria. Outdoor and indoor sports include football, cricket, basketball, volleyball, table tennis, chess and carrom.
cityProfile: MSE is on Gandhi Mandapam Road in Kotturpuram, Chennai, behind the Government Data Centre and Anna Centenary Library. It is a single specialist campus for this profile, not the Central University of Tamil Nadu. Historical university partnerships should not be confused with the location or awarding arrangements for new MSE cohorts.
practicalExposure: The economics portfolio includes quantitative methods, econometrics and specialised applications. The MA programmes include a summer internship after the second semester, while the Data Science programme requires a summer internship and a second-year dissertation. The integrated route adds programming and analytical study. A BA exit within the integrated programme is not an additional admissions route, and applied work does not guarantee employment.
hostelOverview: MSE has separate accommodation for men and women; its integrated-programme brochure describes three girls’ hostels and one boys’ hostel. Hostel rooms remain subject to availability. The hostel page describes dining, common reading facilities, television and internet access.
dietarySupport: The campus mess serves vegetarian and non-vegetarian food, and the cafeteria provides snacks, tea and coffee. Applicants with allergies or other dietary needs should confirm the arrangements directly rather than assume a dedicated service.
safetyOverview: MSE identifies grievance and sexual-harassment prevention, anti-ragging and SC/ST committees. These provide institutional reporting channels; the presence of a committee is not a guarantee against incidents.
studentSupport: The programme brochures identify separate student offices for admissions, including a direct route for foreign self-financing applicants. The campus library and reading rooms support academic work, and the grievance committees provide additional points of contact.
whyChoose: Study economics through five distinct postgraduate specialisations rather than a single undifferentiated MA.
The integrated route provides staged exit awards within a continuous five-year economics curriculum.
Data Science includes both a summer internship and dissertation alongside quantitative and computing study.
thingsToConsider: The 2026 brochures impose programme-specific age, mathematics and academic-score conditions.
Published semester charges include category-specific components; they are not isolated annual tuition totals.
The two MBA sources disagree on important eligibility conditions, which require clarification before applying.
bestFitFor: Applicants comfortable with mathematics and quantitative approaches to economics.
Graduates comparing a specialised MA with an applied data-science master’s degree.
Applicants able to meet the exact academic and age rules of the selected Indian or foreign self-financing route.

faq.question: Which taught programmes are currently advertised?
faq.answer: MSE advertises an integrated MA in Economics, five two-year MA specialisations, MSc Data Science and MBAs in Finance and Business Analytics. Doctoral routes are separate research degrees.

faq.question: Are BA exit awards separate new-entry degrees?
faq.answer: The current integrated economics route has a three-year BA Honours exit and a four-year BA Honours with Research exit. These exits should not be represented as independently advertised new-entry programmes.

faq.question: Can foreign students apply to the economics and data-science programmes?
faq.answer: The 2026 brochures provide a self-financing direct-application route for foreign nationals. The designated MSE office receives the application, bio-data and academic qualifications; programme academic conditions still apply.

faq.question: Is mathematics required?
faq.answer: The integrated route requires Standard, Applied or Business Mathematics at 10+2. The MA and MSc routes require mathematics at 10+2 or equivalent, or qualifying undergraduate mathematical-economics study.

faq.question: Do the fee figures represent annual tuition?
faq.answer: No. The reviewed MSE brochures principally quote semester charges, with separate infrastructure and one-time admission charges. Indian, NRI and foreign-national tariffs differ.

faq.question: Is accommodation available?
faq.answer: MSE has separate men’s and women’s hostels, but availability must be confirmed. Its mess serves vegetarian and non-vegetarian food, with a separate cafeteria for snacks and drinks.

faq.question: Is an English website proof of English-medium teaching?
faq.answer: No. The reviewed programme sources do not explicitly establish the teaching medium. The language field remains unpopulated rather than being inferred from the website or an English curriculum subject.

faq.question: Are the cited dates upcoming admissions deadlines?
faq.answer: No. The MA, integrated MA and MSc brochures concern the 2026 cohort. Their closed dates do not establish a future application window.

programmes.officialTitle: Integrated Master of Arts in Economics

eligibleAudiences: Indian applicants meeting the academic and age requirements
Foreign nationals through the self-financing direct-application route
restrictions: The 2026 academic and age conditions apply; an offer depends on the appropriate selection route.
Foreign applicants submit qualifications and bio-data directly to the designated MSE office; do not assume the Indian entrance-test route applies.

admissionsContent.overview: A five-year integrated economics programme with a three-year BA Honours exit and a four-year BA Honours with Research exit. Indian and foreign self-financing applicants follow different admission procedures.

eligibility.intro: Admission depends on the qualification and applicant-category requirements for this programme.
items: Pass the qualifying 10+2 examination on the first attempt; the 2026 brochure specifies the final 2026 academic-year cohort.
Minimum 65% for General, 60% for OBC-NCL and 50% for SC/ST/PwD applicants, or equivalent grades.
Mathematics at 10+2 is mandatory; Standard, Applied or Business Mathematics is accepted.
Applicants must be under 22 on 1 July 2026.
Foreign applicants meet the same minimum qualifications; obtain AIU equivalence if the qualification is not on its recognised list.

applicationSteps: Check the programme’s exact academic, mathematics and age conditions before applying.
Indian applicants submit the online MSE form and take the designated entrance test.
Foreign self-financing applicants send the prescribed application, bio-data and academic qualifications directly to the designated MSE Students Office.
Complete qualification verification and pay the applicable category-specific fees if selected.

academic: Records establishing the required mathematics study
Attested English translations and AIU equivalence where required for foreign records
